questions.explanation: Ryotwari system was a land revenue system in British India introduced by Thomas Munro which allowed the government to deal directly with the cultivator (‘rhot’) for revenue collection and gave the peasant freedom to seed or acquire new land for cultivation. The Mahalwari system was a land revenue system implemented by the East India Company in 1833 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Madhya Pradesh. This land revenue was implemented on 30% of the land area of India. Before this, the Company had implemented Permanent Settlement in Bengal (in 1793) and Ryotwari in Bombay, Madras etc. (in 1820). Lord Cornwallis introduced the Zamindari System under his Permanent Settlement Act. The three major components of the Zamindari System were – British, Zamindar (Landlord) and peasants. Known as one of the major land revenue systems.
